standard.name: ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English
standard.subtitle: Standard for Technical Documentation
standard.maintainer: ASD Simplified Technical English Maintenance Group
upgradeRequirements: An architecture decision record that accepts the new issue.
A compatibility audit against the previous issue.
A terminology audit of every controlled term.
Checker updates for every changed rule.
A controlled migration of the governed prose.

STE-STRICT.title: Strict profile conformance
STE-STRICT.summary: The final text must obey the LUDWISE ASD-STE100 profile.

STE-DERIVED.title: Derived from a Simplified Technical English baseline
STE-DERIVED.summary: The text starts as a controlled baseline and then passes the user-facing pipeline.

STE-EXEMPT.title: Exempt
STE-EXEMPT.summary: The content is machine syntax, an external value, or text that LUDWISE does not control.

prose.summary: The whole file is controlled prose.

comments.summary: Only the code comments and doc comments in the file are controlled prose.

strings.summary: Only the human-readable string literals in the file are controlled prose.
strings.checkerSupportReason: The extractor reads template text, a visitor-visible attribute and a named string constant. A string that a runtime value composes is reviewed rather than measured.

classification.reason: The design handoff is vendored reference material that LUDWISE did not author.
License text that somebody else wrote. Neither file carries a prose-bearing extension, so the rule states the intent rather than changing a result.
README, security and contribution documents are internal technical prose.
Every document under docs/ is developer or operational prose.
Agent instructions and agent prompts must be unambiguous.
Pull request and issue templates are prose that LUDWISE controls.
Workflow and template files are machine configuration. Phase 2 governs the prose values inside them.
The robots file contains machine-readable crawler directives, not prose.
Recorded transcripts and fixtures are data, not authored prose.
A fixture holds a deliberate violation, so its comments are data rather than authored prose.
A code comment states a contract or a rationale, so it is descriptive prose. A step that a person performs belongs in a runbook, not beside the code.
Most visitor-visible strings are written in a template. src/lib/http/filter-advice.ts is the one module that holds visitor sentences instead.
A tooling comment explains a rationale that the code cannot state. It gives information rather than an instruction.
A test comment records why the assertion is correct. It gives information rather than an instruction.
A configuration comment explains a decision that the value cannot show. It gives information rather than an instruction.
Any other Markdown file in the repository is prose that LUDWISE authored.
The file holds no prose that LUDWISE authored.

blocks.title: YAML front matter
blocks.reason: Front matter is machine-readable metadata, not prose.

blocks.title: Fenced code block
blocks.reason: A code example is programming-language syntax, not prose.

blocks.title: HTML comment in Markdown
blocks.reason: An HTML comment carries tooling directives, not reader-visible prose.

spans.title: Inline code span
spans.reason: Backticks mark an identifier, a command, or a protocol value.

spans.title: Markdown link destination
spans.reason: A link target is a path or a URL. The link text stays under control.

spans.title: URL, URI and mail address
spans.reason: An address is an external value that a rewrite would break.

spans.title: File path and file name
spans.reason: A path names a file on disk and must stay exact.

spans.title: Programming identifier
spans.reason: Function, type, constant, column and environment-variable names must stay exact.

spans.title: Official product and company name
spans.reason: An official name is fixed by its owner.

spans.title: Documentation-comment tag
spans.reason: A tag such as the parameter tag is tooling syntax.

spans.title: Conventional Commit type and scope
spans.reason: The prefix is machine-structured release metadata.

contractions.note: The possessive is never reported. A word such as one's is left out of this list, because the possessive and the contraction cannot be told apart without part-of-speech data.

spelling.reason: ASD-STE100 uses one spelling for one word. LUDWISE writes American English.

punctuation.reason: A slash between two words hides which alternative applies. A path and a date also use a slash, so the checker reports a closed list rather than every slash.

lexicon.reason: LUDWISE holds no permission to a machine-readable copy of the controlled dictionary, and will not scrape one. Until a licensed source exists, LW-STE-WORD-APPROVED and LW-STE-WORD-PART-OF-SPEECH are not run.

causalSince.reason: Issue 9 approves since for time. A clause that gives a reason must read because. No word list separates the two, so the checker reports the shape a reason takes: since opening a sentence, or since after a comma. Since with a date or an event is untouched.
